correctness.rationale: The determinant is Vandermonde times e_2; a singular four-column minor has a one-dimensional left nullspace by degree-four interpolation. Poonen–Rubinstein Theorem 3 exhausts all minimal positive six-root relations: 2+2+2, 3+3, and a primitive 30th-root six-term relation. Graph edge-incidence determines the antipodal pair/ternary coset cases; the unique primitive opposite-edge matching gives exactly two free order-30 orbits. Intersection and stabilizer counting yield all five terms of D(N). The standalone verifier checked the formal polynomial determinant factorization and independently confirmed the structural iff and counts for every four-column set at 19 finite cyclic orders through 60, including 30 and 60. Finite cases alone are not proof of all-N quantification; the cited source theorem and symbolic arguments supply that.

originality.rationale: The exact Schur factor and continuous ambiguity solution families were established in Matter et al. (2021). The new claim is explicitly limited to a closed all-modulus arithmetic count and overlap-corrected orbit census of unordered four-column singular minors, including the isolated two-orbit 30-divisibility phenomenon and rank exactly three; known all-order full-spark yes/no criterion and isolated order-ten enumeration do not imply the stated count without new case enumeration. Residual risk is an equivalent older enumeration extracted from the same continuous-array classification; originality assessed on best available evidence, not declared mathematically proven by searches.

value.rationale: The fixed four-row frame is the established minimal composite-size obstruction to naive full-spark sufficient conditions. Its exact rank-defect count D(N) is a natural sampling reliability invariant, not an arbitrary perturbation. It extends a yes/no full-spark criterion and isolated order-ten examples to all moduli, and reveals and exactly counts a structurally different primitive order-30 family alongside overlap corrections. The motivated complete classification of all rank-deficient four-column samplings and precise ranks are reusable in finite harmonic-frame analysis.
